title: The Ultimate Diet Challenge: Veggies vs. King's Food
paragraphs: So, get this. Three years into King Jehoiakim's rule in Judah, King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon decided to declare war on Jerusalem and basically laid siege to the city. God let King Jehoiakim of Judah get captured, and on top of that, Nebuchadnezzar also snagged some of the valuable stuff from the Temple of God. He took the king and all the goods back to Babylon, which was this ancient place called Shinar, and put all the Temple furnishings in his own sacred treasury.

The king then told Ashpenaz, the guy in charge of the palace staff, to find some of the best and brightest young Israelite men from royal and noble families. He wanted guys who were healthy, good-looking, smart, and well-educated—basically, perfect candidates for leadership roles in his government. The plan was to brainwash them with the Babylonian language and all their magic and fortune-telling nonsense. The king also ordered that they be served the same food as the royal court—the best of the best. After three years of this training, they were supposed to be ready to serve in the king's court.

Four young men from Judah—Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah—were part of this group. The head of the palace staff gave them new Babylonian names: Daniel was now Belteshazzar, Hananiah was Shadrach, Mishael was Meshach, and Azariah was Abednego.

But Daniel was determined not to disrespect himself by eating the king's food or drinking his wine. So, he asked the head of the palace staff to let him off the hook with the royal diet. By God's grace, the head of the staff liked Daniel, but he was still nervous. He warned him, "I'm scared of what the king will do. He's the one who ordered this diet, and if he sees that you're not as healthy as the other guys, he'll literally have my head!"

But Daniel went to the steward who was in charge of him and his friends, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah, and said, "Just test us for ten days. Give us only vegetables and water. Then, compare how we look with the other young men who are eating the royal food. You can decide what to do based on what you see."

The steward was cool with it and gave them vegetables and water for ten days. At the end of the ten days, they looked healthier and stronger than all the others who had been eating from the royal menu. So, the steward kept letting them skip the royal food and drink and just served them vegetables.

God blessed these four young men with incredible knowledge and skill in all sorts of literature and life lessons. On top of that, Daniel had a special gift for understanding all kinds of visions and dreams. When the training period set by the king was over, the head of the royal staff brought all the young men to Nebuchadnezzar. The king interviewed them and found that Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah were way ahead of all the other young men. No one could even compare to them.

And so, they began their service in the king's court. Whenever the king needed advice on anything, whether it was about books or life, he found them to be ten times better than all the magicians and enchanters in his entire kingdom.
Daniel continued to serve the king until the first year of King Cyrus's reign.

title: The King's Crazy Dream & Daniel's God-Tier Reveal

paragraphs: So, in the second year he was king, Nebuchadnezzar started having these wild dreams that were seriously messing with his head. He literally couldn't sleep. So he calls up all his go-to guys—all the Babylonian magicians, enchanters, sorcerers, and psychics—to figure outhat was up with his dreams. When they all showed up and stood in front of him, he was like, 'Yo, I had this dream and it's living rent-free in my head. I'm not sleeping until I know what it means.'
The psychics, speaking in Aramaic, were like, 'Long live the king! Just tell us the dream, and we'll totally break it down for you.'

But the king shot back, 'Nah, here's the deal. If you can't tell me the dream *and* what it means, I'm gonna have you guys ripped to shreds, and your houses will be turned into rubble. But if you can do it, I'll hook you up with tons of gifts and make you famous. So, get to it. Tell me the dream and what it means.'
They tried again, 'Your Majesty, with all due respect, just tell us the dream. We'll give you the interpretation.'

But the king was like, 'I see what you're doing. You're just stalling for time 'cause you know you're toast. You know if you can't tell me the dream, it's game over for you. I see right through your little act. You're just gonna make up some fake story to try and confuse me until I give up. Not happening. First, you tell me the dream, and then I'll know you're for real about the interpretation and not just making stuff up.'

The psychics were shook. 'Literally no one on earth can do what you're asking. No king, no matter how goated, has ever asked for something like this from a magician, enchanter, or psychic. What you're asking is basically impossible unless a god reveals it—and they don't just hang out with us regular people.'

That just made the king even more mad. He totally lost it and ordered all the wise men in Babylon to be executed. When the order went out, Daniel and his friends were on the list too. They were marked to be killed.

When Arioch, the head of the royal guards, was getting ready to carry out the executions, Daniel, being super smart, pulled him aside and quietly asked what was going on. 'Why the sudden death sentence for everyone?'
After Arioch gave him the lowdown, Daniel went straight to the king and asked for a little more time so he could interpret the dream.

Then Daniel went home and told his boys Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah what was happening. He told them to pray to the God of heaven to have mercy and help them solve this mystery so the four of them wouldn't get killed along with all the other wise men in Babylon.
That night, God revealed the secret to Daniel in a vision. Daniel immediately started praising the God of heaven, saying,

'Shoutout to God's name, forever and ever. He knows everything, he does everything. He changes the seasons and directs history. He puts kings in power and takes them down. He gives people intelligence and insight. He reveals deep and secret things, he sees in the dark—he's literally made of light! God of my ancestors, thank you so much! All the praise to you! You made me wise and strong. And now you've shown us what we asked for. You've solved the king's mystery.'
So Daniel went back to Arioch, the guy in charge of the executions. He said, 'Yo, cancel the executions! Take me to the king, and I'll tell him what his dream means.'
Arioch didn't waste a second. He ran to the king with Daniel and said, 'I found a guy from the Jewish exiles who can interpret the king's dream!'
The king asked Daniel (who had a Babylonian name, Belteshazzar), 'Are you for real? You can actually tell me the dream I had and what it means?'

Daniel answered the king, 'No human can solve the king's mystery, it doesn't matter who they are—no wise man, enchanter, magician, or psychic. But there is a God in heaven who solves mysteries, and he has solved this one. He's giving King Nebuchadnezzar a sneak peek of what's going to happen in the future. This is the dream you had when you were lying in bed, the vision that was in your head:

'While you were just chilling on your bed, O king, you started thinking about what's coming in the future. The God who reveals mysteries showed you what will happen. But the interpretation is being given through me, not because I'm smarter than anyone else in the country, but so that you'll know what it means, so you'll understand what you dreamed.'

'What you saw, O king, was this massive statue standing in front of you. It looked super impressive. And honestly, kinda terrifying. The statue's head was pure gold, its chest and arms were silver, its stomach and hips were bronze, its legs were iron, and its feet were a mix of iron and clay. While you were staring at this statue, a rock that was cut out of a mountain by, like, invisible hands, came and hit the statue, smashing its iron and clay feet. Then the whole thing just fell apart—iron, clay, bronze, silver, and gold, all smashed into tiny pieces. It was like dust in an empty lot on a hot summer day, blown away by the wind until there was nothing left. But the rock that hit the statue became a huge mountain that took over the whole horizon. That was your dream.'

'And now, we'll tell you what it means. You, O king, are the most powerful king on earth. The God of heaven has given you everything: rule, power, strength, and glory. He put you in charge of all people, wild animals, and birds, all over the world—you're the top ruler, you're the head of gold. But your kingdom will be taken over by another kingdom, not as great as yours, and that one by a third, a bronze kingdom, that will still rule the whole land. And after that, a fourth kingdom will come, as strong as iron. Just like iron smashes everything to pieces, it will break and crush the kingdoms that came before it.'

'But then the feet and toes that were a mix of clay and iron will turn into a messed-up kingdom with some iron still in it. Just like the toes were part clay and part iron, it'll end up being a mix of breakable and unbreakable. That kingdom won't stick together, any more than iron and clay can mix.'

'But during the time of these kingdoms, the God of heaven will set up a kingdom that will never be destroyed, and no other kingdom will ever take it over. In the end, it will crush all the other kingdoms and finish them off, and it will stand strong forever. It'll be like that rock cut from the mountain by an invisible hand that crushed the iron, the bronze, the clay, the silver, and the gold.'
'The great God has let the king know what will happen in the future. This is the 100% accurate telling of the dream, and the interpretation is also legit.'

When Daniel finished, King Nebuchadnezzar fell on his face, totally in awe of Daniel. He ordered sacrifices and incense to be offered in Daniel's honor. He said to Daniel, 'No cap, your God is the God of all gods, the Master of all kings. And he solves all mysteries, I know, because you've solved this one.'

Then the king gave Daniel a major promotion, showered him with gifts, and made him governor over the whole province of Babylon and the head of all the Babylonian wise men. And because Daniel asked, the king appointed Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego to high-up positions throughout Babylon, while Daniel governed from the royal palace.

title: Refusing to Bow Down? WILD

paragraphs: So, King Nebuchadnezzar had this massive gold statue built—like, 90 feet tall and 9 feet wide. It was huge. He stuck it right in the middle of the Dura plain in Babylon. Then he invited, like, *everyone* important—all the big shots and honored ones—to this huge dedication party for the statue. And of course, they all showed up and stood in front of this giant statue he'd put up.

Then this announcer gets up and shouts, 'Listen up, everybody! No matter who you are or where you're from! As soon as you hear the music start—wwe're talking a full-on orchestra with trumpets, trombones, tubas, baritones, drums, and cymbals—you have to dropo your knees and worship the gold statue King Nebuchadnezzar built. And if you don't? You get tossed straight into a fiery furnace. No joke.'

The music started, and it was this epic band equipped with all the musical instruments of Babylon. And just like that, everyone—literally everyone, from all over—bowed down and worshiped the gold statue the king had set up.

But right then, some Babylonian fortune-tellers went to the king to snitch on the Jews. They were like, 'Hey, King, hope you live forever! You made a rule that everyone had to bow down to the statue when the music played, or they'd get thrown into a furnace, right? Well, these three Jewish guys you put in high positions in the province of Babylon—Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego—are totally ignoring you.hey're not respecting your gods, and they're refusing to worship the gold statue.'

King Nebuchadnezzar was livid. He ordered Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego to be brought to him. When they got there, he asked, 'Is this for real, guys? You're really disrespecting my gods and refusing to worship the statue I made? Look, I'll give you a second chance. When the music plays, you bow down and worship the statue. If you don't, you're going straight into that furnace, and that's final. What god do you think can save you from me then?'

Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego answered King Nebuchadnezzar, 'We're not worried. If you throw us in the fire, the God we serve is more than able to save us from the furnace and anything else you can think of. But even if he doesn't, we want to make it clear, O king, that we're still not going to serve your gods or worship your gold statue. No cap.'

Nebuchadnezzar was so mad his face turned purple. He completely lost it and ordered the furnace to be cranked up seven times hotter than normal. He had some of the strongest soldiers in his army tie up Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, hands and feet, and toss them into the super-hot furnace. Bound hand and foot, fully dressed from head to toe, they were thrown right into the fire. The furnace was so insanely hot because the king was in such a rush that the flames actually killed the soldiers who threw them in. Meanwhile, the fire was just raging around the three guys.
Suddenly, King Nebuchadnezzar jumped up, totally shocked. 'Wait a minute,' he said. 'Didn't we throw three guys in there, all tied up?'
'Yeah, that's right, O king,' they answered.
'But look!' he yelled. 'I see four guys, just walking around in the fire, totally fine! And the fourth one looks like a son of the gods or something!'
Nebuchadnezzar ran to the opening of the furnace and shouted, 'Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, servants of the Most High God, come on out!'
And just like that, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego walked out of the fire.

All the important people, the government officials, and the king's advisors crowded around to check them out. They saw that the fire hadn't so much as touched the three men—not a single hair was burned,their clothes weren't even scorched, and they didn't even smell like smoke.

Nebuchadnezzar said, 'Praise be to the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego! He sent his angel to rescue his servants who trusted him. They defied the king's command and were willing to die rather than serve or worship any god except their own.'

'So, I'm making a new rule: Anyone, anywhere, from any background, who says anything bad about the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego will be torn apart, and their house will be demolished. There's no other god who can pull off a rescue like that.'
Then the king gave Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego a big promotion in Babylon.

paragraphs: Yo, what's up world! This is King Nebuchadnezzar, sending this out to everyone, everywhere—no matter who you are or where you're from. Hope you're all living your best life. I gotta tell you about the seriously mind-blowing miracles the Most High God did for me.
His miracles are insane, and the stuff He does is just wild. His kingdom is forever, and His rule never stops.

So, I, Nebuchadnezzar, was just chilling at my palace, totally relaxed and living the good life. But then, I had this dream while I was in bed that totally freaked me out—it was a straight-up nightmare. So I called all the wise guys in Babylon to come and tell me what it meant. WWhen they all showed up—the magicians, the psychics, the fortune-tellers, the witches, all of them—I told them the dream.t none of them had a clue.
Then Daniel came in. His Babylonian name is Belteshazzar, named after my own god, and this dude is full of the divine Holy Spirit. So I told him my dream.
"Belteshazzar," I said, "you're the head of all the magicians, and I know you're filled with the Holy Spirit, so no mystery is too hard for you. Check out this dream I had and tell me what's up."

"So, I was lying in bed and I saw this huge tree right in the middle of the world. As I watched, it got massive and super strong. Its top literally touched the sky, and you could see it from the four corners of the Earth. Its leaves were gorgeous, and it had so much fruit—enough for everyone! Wild animals were chilling under it, birds had nests in its branches, and basically everything was fed and protected by it."
"Then, still in my dream, I saw a holy messenger come down from heaven and yell:"

"'Cut down the tree, chop off its branches, strip its leaves, and scatter its fruit. Get all the animals out from under it and the birds out of its branches. But leave the stump and roots in the ground, tied up with iron and bronze in the middle of a field.'"
"'Let him get soaked with dew from the sky and eat with the animals. Let him totally lose his mind and get the brain of an animal instead, and let this go on for seven years.'"

"The angels are making this official, the holy messengers are delivering the message, so that everyone alive will know that the Most High God is the one in charge of all human kingdoms. He can set up kingdoms however He wants and can make leaders out of complete nobodies."

"So that was the dream I, King Nebuchadnezzar, had. Now it's your turn, Belteshazzar—tell me what it means. None of the other wise guys in Babylon could figure it out, but I know you can. You're full of the Holy Spirit."
At first, Daniel, who they called Belteshazzar in Babylon, was pretty shaken up. The thoughts flooding his mind were terrifying.
"Belteshazzar," the king said, "it's cool. Don't let the dream and what it means freak you out."
"My king," Belteshazzar said, "I really wish this dream was about your enemies and not you."

"That tree you saw that grew so huge and strong, with its top in the sky, visible from the four corners of the world; the tree with the amazing leaves and tons of fruit for everyone; the tree where animals took shelter and birds built nests—that tree is you, O king."
"You've become great and powerful. Your royal awesomeness reaches the sky, and your rule extends to every corner of the world."

"But the part about the holy angel coming down from heaven and saying, 'Cut down the tree, destroy it, but leave the stump and roots in the ground tied up with iron and bronze in the field; let him be soaked with dew from the sky and eat with the animals for seven years'—that's also about you, my king. It means the Most High God has laid down this sentence for you: You'll be kicked out of society and have to live with wild animals. You'll eat grass like a cow. You'll be soaked with dew from the sky. This will happen for seven years, and you'll learn that the Most High God is the one who rules over all human kingdoms and can put anyone He wants in charge."
"The part about leaving the stump and roots means your kingdom will still be here for you after you learn that heaven is in control."
"So, king, listen to my advice: Ditch your sins and start doing good for others. Stop your wicked ways and start caring for the poor and needy. Then your good life will continue."

All of this actually happened to King Nebuchadnezzar. Just twelve months later, he was walking on the balcony of his royal palace in Babylon and bragging, "Look at this amazing city of Babylon! I built it all by myself as a royal palace to show off my honor and glory!"

He had barely finished speaking when a voice from heaven said, "This is the final word on you, King Nebuchadnezzar: Your kingdom is being taken from you. You will be driven away from people and will live with wild animals. You will eat grass like a cow. This will last for seven years, enough time for you to learn that the Most High God rules over all human kingdoms and puts whoever He wants in charge."
It happened instantly. Nebuchadnezzar was kicked out of society, ate grass like a cow, and got soaked with dew from the sky. His hair grew long like eagle feathers and his nails grew like hawk claws.
"After seven years, I, Nebuchadnezzar, looked up to heaven. My sanity was restored, and I praised the Most High God, thanking and glorifying the One who lives forever:"
"'His rule is eternal, His kingdom never ends. Life on earth is pretty insignificant, but God's army in heaven keeps everything in order. No one can stop Him or question His authority.'"

"The moment my mind came back, I also got back my majesty and splendor, making my kingdom shine again. All the leaders and important people came to find me. I was put back on the throne, and I became even greater than before. And that's why I'm singing—I, Nebuchadnezzar—singing and praising the King of Heaven:"
"'Everything He does is right, and He does it perfectly. He knows how to humble a proud person.'"

title: The Writing on the Wall Gets Real

splits.note: 가독성 목적의 Teen 문단 분할 — MSG 대비 내용 손실·추가·오역 없음, EN/KO 문단 수·배지·의미 일치 확인됨 (2026-09-24 다니엘 감사, 스탠딩 승인 규칙 적용)

paragraphs: So, King Belshazzar threw this massive party for a thousand of his honored ones. The wine was flowing like crazy. Belshazzar, feeling buzzed, randomly ordered the gold and silver cups that his dad, Nebuchadnezzar, had jacked from God's Temple in Jerusalem. He wanted to drink from them with his crew, his wives, and his concubines. When they brought out the fancy cups, the king, his boys, his wives, and his concubines all started drinking wine from them. They drank and drunkenly cheered for their own gods—idols made of gold, silver, bronze, iron, wood, and stone.

Then, out of nowhere, the fingers of a human hand just appeared and started writing on the palace wall, which was all lit up by a lamp. When the king saw this disembodied hand writing, he went totally pale, like he'd seen a ghost, and freaked out. His legs turned to jelly and his knees were literally knocking together. He screamed for his magic guys, the fortune-tellers, and the psychics to come over. He told these Babylonian wizards, “Yo, anyone who can read this writing and tell me what it means will get famous and rich—I'm talking a purple robe, a fat gold chain—and you'll be the third most powerful person in the kingdom.”

They all tried, one by one, but nobody could make sense of it. They couldn't read the writing or explain it to the king. So now the king was even more scared. He looked like all the blood had drained from his face. His honored ones were all in a panic.

Then the queen heard about the king and his nobles losing their minds and came into the banquet hall. She was like, “Long live the king! Don’t get all worked up. Don’t just sit there looking terrified. There’s a guy in your kingdom who’s literally full of the Holy Spirit. Back in your dad's day, he was famous for being a genius with spiritual wisdom. He was so legit that your dad, King Nebuchadnezzar, put him in charge of all the magicians, enchanters, fortune-tellers, and psychics. There was no one like him. He could do anything—explain dreams, solve mysteries, figure out puzzles. His name is Daniel, but the king nicknamed him Belteshazzar. Get Daniel in here. He’ll tell you what’s going on.”

So they brought Daniel in. The king asked him, “Are you Daniel, one of the Jewish exiles my dad brought from Judah? I’ve heard about you—that you’re full of the Holy Spirit, that you have a brilliant mind, and that you're incredibly wise. We brought in the wise men and enchanters to read this writing on the wall and explain it to me. They couldn’t figure it out—not a single word. But I’ve heard that you can interpret dreams and solve mysteries. So, if you can read this and tell me what it means, you’ll be rich and famous—a purple robe, a big gold chain around your neck—and you'll be third-in-command in the kingdom.”
Daniel replied to the king, “You can keep your gifts, or give them to someone else. But I’ll read the writing for you and tell you what it means.”

“Listen up, O king! The Most High God gave your father Nebuchadnezzar a huge kingdom and a legendary reputation. Because God made him so famous, people from all over, no matter their race or religion, were totally scared of him. He could kill or spare people just because he felt like it. He’d promote or demote people on a whim. He got a huge ego and a hard heart. Then God knocked him off his high horse and took away his fame. He was kicked out of society, lost his mind, and lived like a wild animal. He ate grass like a cow and got soaked by heaven's dew until he finally learned his lesson: that the Most High God is the one who rules over human kingdoms and can put anyone he wants in charge.

“You’re his son and you knew all this, but you’re just as arrogant as he was. Look at you, trying to compete with the Lord of heaven! You had the holy cups from his Temple brought to your drunk party so you and your friends, your wives, and your concubines could drink from them. You used the sacred cups to toast your gods of silver and gold, bronze and iron, wood and stone—gods that are blind, deaf, and dumb. But you dissed the living God who holds your entire life in his hands, from start to finish.
“That’s why God sent the hand that wrote on the wall, and this is what it says: MENE, TEQEL, and PERES. And this is what the words mean:
“Mene: God has counted the days of your rule, and they’re all used up.
“Teqel: You’ve been weighed on the scales, and you’re seriously lacking.
“Peres: Your kingdom has been split up and handed over to the Medes and Persians.”
Belshazzar did what he promised. He gave Daniel a purple robe, put the big gold chain around his neck, and made him the third most powerful person in the kingdom.
That very same night, the Babylonian king Belshazzar was murdered. Darius the Mede, who was sixty-two, took over as king.

paragraphs: So, King Darius decided to switch things up in his kingdom. He set up 120 governors to run things everywhere. On top of them, he put three main bosses, and guess who was one of them? Daniel. The governors had to report to these bosses, who kept everything running smoothly for the king. But Daniel? He was on another level. He was so smart and had such a great attitude that he totally showed up the other bosses and governors. The king saw this and was like, "Yo, I'm putting this guy in charge of everything."

The other bosses and governors got super jealous and started trying to dig up some dirt on Daniel to use against him. But they couldn't find anything. He was a total stand-up guy, super trustworthy. There was zero evidence of him slacking off or doing anything shady. So they finally gave up and were like, "Ugh, we're never gonna get this guy unless we make it about his religion."

The vice-regents and governors all ganged up, went to the king, and said, "King Darius, hope you live forever! All of us—your top officials, governors, and leaders—had a meeting and we think you should make a new rule:
For the next 30 days, nobody is allowed to pray to any god or person except for you, O king. Anyone who breaks this rule gets thrown into the lions' den.
"You should totally make this an official decree, O king. Make it a law that can't be changed, like the laws of the Medes and Persians."
So, King Darius signed the new law.

When Daniel heard the law was official, he just kept doing what he always did. He went home to his upstairs room where the windows opened toward Jerusalem. Three times a day, he got on his knees and prayed, thanking and praising his God, no cap.

The haters came and found him praying and asking God for help. They went straight to the king and were like, "Hey, remember that decree you signed? The one that said for 30 days, no one could pray to anyone but you, or they'd be thrown into the lions' den?"
"Absolutely," the king said. "It's a done deal, written in stone, like all the laws of the Medes and Persians."
Then they dropped the bomb: "Well, Daniel, one of the Jewish exiles, is totally ignoring you and your law, O king. He's still praying three times a day."
Hearing this, the king was seriously bummed out. He spent the whole rest of the day trying to figure out a way to save Daniel from the mess he'd created.
But then the haters came back and said, "Remember, O king, the law of the Medes and Persians says that a king's decree can never be changed."
The king finally gave in and ordered them to bring Daniel and throw him into the lions' den. But he said to Daniel, "Your God, the one you're so loyal to, is gonna get you out of this."
A huge stone was put over the opening of the den. The king sealed it with his own ring and the rings of all his nobles, so nobody could change Daniel's fate.
The king went back to his palace but was in no mood to eat. He couldn't sleep at all and just fasted all night.

First thing in the morning, the king got up and rushed to the lions' den. As he got close, he called out, super worried, "Daniel, servant of the living God, has your God, the one you serve so faithfully, saved you from the lions?"
"Long live the king!" Daniel shouted back. "My God sent his angel, and he shut the lions' mouths so they couldn't hurt me. God knows I'm innocent, and I've never done anything to wrong you, O king."
When the king heard this, he was overjoyed. He ordered them to get Daniel out of the den. When they pulled him up, he didn't have a single scratch on him. He had trusted his God, for real.

Then the king ordered that the guys who had ratted on Daniel be thrown into the lions' den, along with their wives and kids. Before they even hit the ground, the lions were all over them, tearing them to pieces. It was brutal.
Then King Darius sent out this message to people of every race, color, and belief all over the world:

"Hope you're all living in peace! I'm making a new rule that in every part of my kingdom, everyone must respect and fear the God of Daniel. He is the living God who lives forever. His kingdom will never be destroyed. His rule is eternal. He's a savior and a rescuer. He does insane miracles in heaven and on earth. He's the one who saved Daniel from the power of the lions."
From then on, Daniel was a big deal during Darius's reign, and also when the next king, Cyrus the Persian, took over.

title: Daniel's Epic Nightmare About Four Wild Beasts

splits.note: 가독성 목적의 Teen 문단 분할 — MSG 대비 내용 손실·추가·오역 없음, EN/KO 문단 수·배지·의미 일치 확인됨 (2026-09-24 다니엘 감사, 스탠딩 승인 규칙 적용)

paragraphs: So, back in the first year King Belshazzar was ruling Babylon, Daniel had this dream that was straight-up terrifying. Like, a full-on nightmare. He wrote it all down:
“In my dream, I saw the four winds of heaven making the sea go totally wild. Then, four massive beasts, all looking super different, came up out of the water.

“The first beast was like a lion, but with eagle wings. As I was watching, its wings got ripped off. Then it was forced to stand on two feet like a person, and it was given a human heart. Wild, right?
“Then I saw a second beast that looked like a bear. It was stumbling around with three ribs in its mouth. A voice told it, ‘Go get ‘em! Eat your fill!’
“Next up was another beast, this one like a panther. It had four bird-like wings on its back and four heads. This thing was made to be in charge.

“After that, a fourth beast showed up, and this one was low-key horrifying. It had massive iron teeth and just crushed and ate everything. Whatever was left, it stomped on. This one was a whole different level of monster. And it had ten horns.

“I was just staring at the horns, trying to figure them out, when another little horn popped up. Three of the first horns were yanked out to make space for it. This little horn had human-like eyes and a big mouth that was saying some really arrogant stuff.
“As I was watching all this,

“Thrones were set up and the Ancient One sat down. His clothes were white as snow, and his hair was like white wool. His throne was literally on fire, with blazing wheels. A river of fire was flowing from the throne. Thousands and thousands of angels were serving him, and tens of thousands were attending him. The court was in session, and the books were opened.

“I kept watching. The little horn was still talking all that trash. Then, I saw the monster get killed and its body thrown into a huge fire. The other beasts got to live a bit longer, but they had no power.

“Then in my dream, I saw someone who looked like a human, a son of man, coming on the clouds. He went to the Ancient One and was brought right up to him. He was given all the power and glory to rule. People from every race and nation had to serve him. His rule would last forever, no cap. His kingdom would never be destroyed.

“But honestly, I, Daniel, was seriously disturbed. These visions had me all kinds of agitated. So I went up to one of the guys standing there and asked him what it all meant. And he broke it down for me:
“‘These four huge beasts,’ he said, ‘are four kingdoms that will rise up on earth. But in the end, the holy people of the Most High God will get the kingdom and keep it forever and ever.’

“But I needed to know more. I was super curious about the fourth beast, the one that was so different, the terrifying one with iron teeth and bronze claws that ate everything and stomped on the rest. And I wanted to know about the ten horns and the new little horn that popped up and took out three of the others. This new horn had eyes and a big, arrogant mouth and was the new top dog. I watched it attack God's people and win. But then the Ancient One stepped in and ruled in favor of God's people. In the end, they took over the kingdom.

“The guy kept explaining: ‘The fourth beast is a fourth kingdom that will show up on earth. It’ll be different from the others, a total monster kingdom that will chew up and spit out everyone. The ten horns are ten kings that will come from this kingdom. But then another king will show up, and he'll be different. He'll start by taking down three kings. Then he'll say blasphemous things against the Most High God, go after God's followers, and try to change all the sacred laws and traditions. God's people will be in his power for a time, two times, and half a time.’

“‘But when the court is in session, that horn will lose all its power and be completely destroyed. Then the rule and authority and glory of all the kingdoms on earth will be given to the people of the Most High God. Their kingdom will last forever. All other rulers will serve and obey them.’
“And that was the end of the dream. I, Daniel, was in shock. I felt like I'd seen a ghost. But I kept it all to myself.”

title: Crazy Animal Battle Royale?! Here's the Deets
paragraphs: So, back in the third year of King Belshazzar's reign, I, Daniel, had another vision. This was round two for me.

In the vision, I was in Susa, the main city in the Elam province, just chilling by the Ulai Canal. Then I look over and, whoa, there's this ram just standing by the gate. This ram had two massive horns, one was bigger than the other, but the bigger one grew in last which was kinda weird. Then I watched this ram just go wild, charging first west, then north, then south. Literally no other animal could stop it. It was doing whatever it wanted, walking around like it owned the place, the king of all animals.

While I was watching this, trying to figure out what was going on, a billy goat with this giant horn right in the middle of its forehead came flying out of the west. It was moving so fast it didn't even touch the ground. This goat went straight for the two-horned ram I saw earlier and, full of rage, just charged it. I saw it, completely furious, slam into the ram and break both its horns clean off. The ram didn't stand a chance. The billy goat threw the ram to the ground and just stomped all over it. Nothing could've saved the ram from that goat.

Then the billy goat got HUGE. But at its peak power, its massive horn broke off, and four other big horns grew in its place, pointing north, south, east, and west. And then from one of those big horns, another horn sprouted. It started out small but grew crazy big, pointing south and east—towards the beautiful land of Palestine. This horn grew so tall it reached the stars, the heavenly army, and it threw some of the stars down to earth and stomped on them. It even had the nerve to challenge God, the Prince of the whole celestial army! Then it got rid of the daily worship and trashed the Sanctuary. As a punishment for their sin, God's holy people got treated the same way as the daily worship. The horn threw God's Truth away. It was super arrogant and took over everything and everyone.
Then I heard two holy angels talking. One asked, 'How long is this gonna last—the daily worship being gone, this awful judgment for sin, God's holy people and the Sanctuary getting disrespected?'
The other one answered, 'It'll be for 2,300 evening and morning sacrifices. Then the Sanctuary will be made right again.'
While I, Daniel, was trying to process what I was seeing, suddenly a figure that looked like a human was standing in front of me.

Then I heard a man's voice from over by the Ulai Canal yell, 'Gabriel, tell this guy what's going on. Explain the vision to him.' He came over to me, but when he got close I got so scared I fell flat on my face.
He said, 'You need to understand, this vision is about the end times.' As soon as he said that, I passed out, face in the dirt. But he picked me up and got me back on my feet.
And then he kept going, 'I want to tell you what's going to happen when the angry judgment days are wrapping up, because all of this is going to have an end.'

'The ram with two horns you saw represents the two kings of the Medes and Persians. The billy goat is the kingdom of the Greeks. The huge horn on its forehead is the first Greek king. The four horns that grew after it broke are the four kings that come after him, but they won't be as powerful.'

'When their kingdoms are losing steam and rebellions are starting up, a king will appear. He'll be tough-looking and a master of tricks. His power will get crazy big. He'll talk a big game, super arrogant, doing whatever he wants, taking out heroes and holy people left and right. He'll scheme to make crime popular—and wow, will it be popular! He'll think he's invincible and get rid of anyone in his way. But when he tries to take on the Prince of all princes, he'll be totally crushed—but not by any human.' This vision of the 2,300 sacrifices, evening and morning, is legit but it's a secret. Keep it to yourself. It's about the distant future.'

I, Daniel, was just walking around in a daze, feeling sick for days. Then I finally got myself together and went back to my job working for the king. But I was still really bothered by the vision. I just couldn't figure it out.

title: Daniel's Epic Prayer & A Wild Prophecy

splits.note: 가독성 목적의 Teen 문단 분할 — MSG 대비 내용 손실·추가·오역 없음, EN/KO 문단 수·배지·의미 일치 확인됨 (2026-09-24 다니엘 감사, 스탠딩 승인 규칙 적용)

paragraphs: “‘So, in the first year that Darius—son of Ahasuerus, born a Mede—became king over Babylon, I, Daniel, was digging into the Scriptures. I was trying to figure out how long Jerusalem would lie in ruins, the number God gave the prophet Jeremiah: seventy years.

So I turned to the Master God, asking for answers—praying hard, skipping meals, wearing rough burlap like I was in mourning, and kneeling in ashes. I just poured out my heart, baring my soul to God, my God:

‘O Master, great and awesome God! You never break your covenant promises, never give up on the people who love you and do what you say. But we’ve sinned in every way you can think of. We’ve done evil stuff, rebelled, dodged your signs and taken detours around your clearly marked paths. We straight-up ignored your servants the prophets, who preached your Word to our kings and leaders, our parents, and everyone in the land. You’ve done everything right, Master, but all we’ve got to show for our lives is guilt and shame—the whole crew: people of Judah, Jerusalem citizens, Israelites at home and in exile, scattered everywhere because we betrayed you. Yeah, God, we’ve been totally exposed in our shame, all of us—our kings, leaders, parents—in front of the whole world. And honestly? We deserved it, because of our sin.’

‘Our only hope is compassion—your compassion, Master, our God—because in our rebellion we gave up all our rights. We didn’t listen when you told us how to live, the clear teaching that came through your servants the prophets. All of us in Israel ignored what you said. We defied your instructions and just did whatever we wanted. And now we’re paying for it: that solemn curse written plainly in your revelation to Moses, your servant, is doing its thing right now among us—that’s the paycheck for our sin against you. You did to us and our rulers exactly what you said you would: you brought this total disaster on us, the worst disaster ever recorded—and it hit Jerusalem!’

‘Just like it was written in your revelation to Moses, the catastrophe was total. Nothing was held back. We just kept on sinning, never gave you a second thought, totally oblivious to your clear warning, so you had no choice but to let the disaster loose on us at full force. You, our God, had every right to do this, since we kept ignoring you on purpose, defiantly.’

‘Master, you are our God—you brought your people out of Egypt in this insane show of power, and people are still talking about it! We admit it: we’ve sinned, we’ve lived bad lives. So please, in line with how you’ve always set things right, stop being so angry at Jerusalem—your own city, your holy mountain. We know this is all our fault, because of our sins and our parents’ sins, and now we’re a total embarrassment to everyone around us, a blot on the whole neighborhood. So God, listen to this determined prayer from your servant. Have mercy on your ruined Sanctuary. Act out of who YOU are, not out of what we are.’

‘Turn your ears our way, God, and listen. Open your eyes and take a long, hard look at our ruined city—this city that’s named after you. We know we don’t deserve to even get a hearing from you. Our only appeal is to your compassion. This prayer is our last and only hope:’
‘Master, listen to us! Master, forgive us! Master, look at us and DO something! Master, don’t put us off! Your city and your people carry your name—you’ve got skin in the game with us!’

While I was still pouring out my heart, confessing my sins and the sins of my people Israel, praying my guts out before my God, interceding for the holy mountain of my God—while I was deep in this prayer, Gabriel, the humanlike guy I’d seen in an earlier vision, came flying toward me like a bird, right around the time of evening worship.

He stood in front of me and said, ‘Daniel, I’ve come to make things crystal clear to you. You had barely started praying when the answer was already given. And now I’m here to deliver it to you. You are so loved! So listen up to the answer, the plain meaning of what’s been revealed:’

‘Seventy sevens are set for your people and your holy city: to put rebellion in a chokehold, stop sin, wipe out crime, set things right forever, confirm what the prophet saw, and anoint the Holy of Holies.’

‘Here’s what you need to get: from the time the word goes out to rebuild Jerusalem until the Anointed Leader shows up, there will be seven sevens. The actual rebuilding will take sixty-two sevens—streets built, moats dug—and those will be rough times. After the sixty-two sevens, the Anointed Leader will be killed—that’s the end of him. The city and the Sanctuary will get wrecked by the army of the new leader rolling in. The end will come rushing in like a flood. War will rage all the way to the end, and desolation will be the order of the day.’

‘Then for one seven, he’ll forge a bunch of strong alliances with lots of people, but halfway through that seven he’ll banish worship and prayers. At the place of worship, a desecrating obscenity will be set up and it’ll stay there—until finally the desecrator himself gets decisively destroyed.’

title: This Angelic Battle is Next Level

paragraphs: So, in the third year that King Cyrus of Persia was in charge, a message was dropped on Daniel, whose Babylonian name was Belteshazzar. And this message was legit, no cap. It was about a huge war, and he totally got what it meant because it was like a divine download.

For three whole weeks, I, Daniel, was super bummed about Jerusalem. I was on a super basic diet—no fancy food, no seasoning, no meat, no wine.I didn't even shower or shave until the three weeks were over.

On the 24th day of the first month, I was just chilling by the great Tigris River. I looked up, and you won't believe it—there was this guy dressed in linen with a solid gold belt. He was totally ripped and glowing, like a living statue, his face was shining, and his eyes were like lasers. His arms and feet looked like polished bronze, and his voice? It was deep and sounded like a whole choir singing at once. It was wild.

I, Daniel, was the only one who saw this vision. The guys with me didn't see it, but they totally freaked out and bounced, hiding because they thought something bad was about to go down. So I was left all alone, and after seeing that, I was literally shaking, and all the color drained from my face.
I heard his voice, and the sound of it made me pass out, face-first in the dirt. Then a hand touched me and pulled me up to my hands and knees.
'Daniel,' he said, 'you're a real one. Listen up to what I'm about to tell you. And get on your feet. Stand at attention. I was sent to give you the scoop.'
When he said that, I stood up, but I was still trembling.

'Chill, Daniel,' he went on, 'don't be scared. The moment you decided to get humble and try to understand, your prayer was heard, and I headed your way. But I got held up by the angel-prince of Persia for a solid three weeks. Then Michael, one of the top-dog angel-princes, came to back me up. I left him there to deal with the Persian prince. And now I'm here to help you understand what's gonna happen to your people down the line. This vision is all about the future.'

While he was explaining all this, I just stared at the ground, speechless. Then, out of nowhere, something like a human hand touched my lips. I opened my mouth and started talking to the messenger: 'Master, when I saw you, I was totally freaked out. My legs felt like jelly. I was frozen. How can a regular dude like me even talk to you, my master? I can't move. I can barely even breathe!'
Then this human-like figure touched me again and gave me strength. He said, 'Don't be afraid, my guy. Peace. It's all gonna be okay. Be strong. You got this.'
As he was saying that, I felt this new strength bubble up inside me. I said, 'Go on, my master, speak. You've given me the courage.'

He said, 'Do you know why I came to you? I have to go back and fight the angel-prince of Persia. And after I'm done with him, the angel-prince of Greece is gonna show up. But first, let me tell you what's written in the Book of Truth. And for the record, the only one who has my back in this fight is Michael, your angel-prince.'

title: Prophecy Drop: North vs. South, Who Will Win?
paragraphs: “‘And for my part, I’ve been backing him up and keeping him strong since the first year Darius the Mede was in charge.’

“‘But now, let me spill the tea on what’s really going down: Three more kings are gonna pop up in Persia, and then a fourth one will show up, way richer than all of them. Once he feels all high and mighty because of his cash, he’s gonna try and pick a fight with the entire kingdom of Greece.

“‘Then, this super powerful king will roll in, take over a massive territory, and basically do whatever he wants. But right when he’s at the peak of his game, thinking he’s got it all on lock, his kingdom will get split into four, like north, south, east, and west. But his own kids won’t get any of it. His royal line will be totally cut off. Other people will just swoop in, tear it apart, and take what they can for themselves.

“‘Next up, the king of the south will get really strong, but one of his own generals will get even stronger and end up ruling a bigger kingdom. After a few years, the two of them will make a deal, and the daughter of the southern king will marry the northern king to make the peace treaty official. But her power won’t last, and her kid won’t make it either. She, her crew, her child, and her husband will all get totally betrayed.

“‘A while later, someone from her royal family will show up to take his place. He’ll lead his army to invade the northern king’s fortress and score a huge W. He’ll take all their fake gods and all the fancy gold and silver stuff that goes with them and haul it all back to Egypt. After a while, the northern king will bounce back and try to invade the south, but it’ll be a total fail. He’ll have to retreat.
“‘But then his sons will get a massive army together and come rushing down like a flood, hitting the south’s defenses with a crazy, all-out attack.

“‘The southern king, totally furious, will come out to fight the northern king and his huge army, and he’ll completely own them. After they clear away all the bodies, the king, high on the victory, will go on a crazy killing spree, taking out tens of thousands. But his win won’t last. The northern king will just build another army, even bigger than the last one, and after a few years, he’ll be back for a rematch with his giant army and tons of supplies.

“‘During that time, a bunch of other people will jump in and fight against the king of the south. Some hotheads from your own people, all hyped up on their own dreams, will join them. But they’ll just fizzle out and fail.

“‘When the king of the north shows up, he’ll set up a siege and capture the main fortress city. The southern armies will just crumble in front of him. Even their elite special forces won’t be able to stop him. He’ll just walk in like he owns the place. He’ll take over that beautiful land, Palestine, and just make himself at home. Then he’ll try to get everything under his control. He’ll propose a peace treaty and even give his own daughter to the southern king in marriage as part of a plot to destroy him. But the whole plan will backfire. It won’t work.

“‘Later, he’ll turn his attention to the coastal areas and take a bunch of prisoners, but some general will step in and shut down his whole bullying operation. The bully will get bullied! He’ll go back home to handle his own stuff, but by then, he’s basically washed up and you won’t hear from him again.
“‘He'll be replaced by a total loser, his rule, reputation, and authority already in shreds. And he won’t be around for long. He’ll just disappear from history without any drama or a big fight.

“‘A total reject will take his place, a guy who was looked down on and never got a promotion. He’ll shock everyone by coming out of nowhere and grabbing the kingdom. He’ll be like a steamroller, just crushing anyone who gets in his way. Even the Prince of the Covenant will be taken down. After they agree to a truce, he’ll break the terms. With just a small crew, he’ll take complete control. He’ll just randomly invade the richest areas. He’ll be worse than any of his ancestors, just stealing and looting the country, living it up with his friends in total luxury.

“‘He’ll make plans to attack the fortress cities, but they’ll be super shortsighted. He’ll get a big army together, all pumped to fight the king of the south. The southern king will respond by getting his own, even bigger army ready. But he won’t be able to keep it up for long because of some shady stuff happening behind the scenes. His own court is full of backstabbers. His army will get wrecked, and the battlefield will be covered in bodies.

“‘The two kings, both secretly plotting against each other, will sit down at a peace talk and just lie to each other’s faces. The treaty will be a total sham and nothing will come of it. But the story isn’t over yet. There’s more.
“‘The king of the north will head home with a ton of loot, but on his way, he’ll be dead-set on disrespecting the holy covenant.

“‘A year later, he’ll invade the south again. But this second time won’t be like the first. When Roman ships show up, he’ll chicken out and run back home. But on his way through the country, he’ll be furious about the holy covenant. He’ll team up with anyone who betrays the covenant, giving them special treatment. His own guards will march in and totally desecrate the Sanctuary and the citadel. They’ll stop the daily worship and put up this disgusting, sacrilegious thing in its place. The northern king will suck up to the covenant-betrayers, making them even more corrupt with his smooth talk, but the people who stay loyal to their God will stand strong and fight back.

“‘The wise leaders will teach the people what’s right by their own example. But they’ll go through some serious trials for a while: some will be killed, some burned, some forced to leave their homes, some robbed. When things get really bad, they’ll get a little help, but not much. A lot of the people helping will be faking it. This whole testing period will be to refine, cleanse, and purify the ones who stay true, because there’s still more to come.

“‘Meanwhile, the king of the north will just do whatever he wants. He’ll get a huge ego and act like he’s greater than any god. He’ll even brag and boast against the God of all gods. And he’ll get away with it for a bit—until the time of judgment is over, because what’s meant to happen will happen. He won’t respect the gods of his ancestors, not even the one that was super popular with the ladies, Adonis. He’ll look down on every god and goddess and hype himself up to be greater than all of them. He’ll even disrespect the God of the holy ones. In God’s own temple, he’ll set up a shrine to some new god nobody’s ever heard of, showing it off with a ton of silver, gold, and jewels. Fighting for this strange god, he’ll attack the main fortresses. He’ll give promotions to everyone who joins his side, giving them power and paying them off with land.

“‘In the final part of this story, the king of the south will challenge him. But the king of the north will come at him like a tornado, with chariots, horses, and a whole fleet of ships, destroying everything in his way. When he enters the beautiful land, people will fall before him like dominoes. Only Edom, Moab, and a few Ammonites will get away. As he goes around conquering country after country, not even Egypt will be safe. He’ll take all of Egypt’s gold, silver, and other treasures. The Libyans and Ethiopians will join his side. But then, he’ll hear some bad news from the north and east that will make him panic. He’ll get super angry and rush off to crush the threat. But right after he sets up his royal camp between the Mediterranean Sea and the Holy Mountain, he’ll meet his end. And there will be literally no one there to help him.’”

title: The Wildest Ending Ever (No Cap)

splits.note: 가독성 목적의 Teen 문단 분할 — MSG 대비 내용 손실·추가·오역 없음, EN/KO 문단 수·배지·의미 일치 확인됨 (2026-09-24 다니엘 감사, 스탠딩 승인 규칙 적용)

paragraphs: “‘So, that’s when Michael, the super powerful angel-prince who’s got your people’s back, is gonna show up. It’s gonna be a time of major trouble, like, the worst the world has ever seen, no cap. But your people? They’ll be saved. Every single person whose name is in the Book will make it through.
A bunch of people who’ve been dead and buried for ages will wake up. Some will get eternal life, which is goated, but others will face eternal shame, which is a huge L.

“‘The people who lived wisely and did good stuff will shine super brightly, like a clear night sky full of stars. And those who helped others find the right way to live will glow like stars forever and ever.

“‘Okay, so this is some top-secret info, Daniel. For your eyes only. You gotta keep it secret and lock up this book until the very end. In the meantime, people are gonna be running around like crazy, trying to figure out what’s even happening.’

As I, Daniel, was trying to process all this, two other guys appeared. One was on this side of the river, and the other was on the opposite bank. One of them asked a third guy, who was dressed in linen and standing over the river, ‘Yo, how long is this crazy story gonna last?’

The guy in linen over the river lifted both his hands to the sky. I heard him make a super serious promise in the name of the Eternal One. He said it would be for a time, two times, and half a time. And when the one oppressing the holy people is finally taken down, the story will be over.
I heard all that, but I was lowkey confused. So I asked, ‘Sir, can you break that down for me?’

‘Just go on with your life, Daniel,’ he said. ‘The message is confidential and locked up until the end, right before things are about to wrap up. The people will be cleansed and made totally new. But the wicked people will just keep being wicked, completely clueless about what’s going on. The ones who live wisely will get it, though.’
“‘From the moment the daily worship at the Temple is stopped and that disgusting, disrespectful thing is set up, it’ll be 1,290 days.
“‘Big shoutout to those who wait patiently and make it through the 1,335 days.
“‘And you? Just do your thing without stressing. Relax. When it’s all said and done, you’ll be back on your feet to get your reward.’”
